Regina Coeli Catholic Primary School
Welcome to Our School
Regina Coeli Catholic Primary School is a Voluntary Aided Primary School within the Archdiocese of Southwark and in partnership with the London Borough of Croydon. The school is usually oversubscribed – it has a maximum of 420 pupils with approximately 30 pupils per class. The school, which has strong Catholic tradition, serves four main parishes within South Croydon and Selsdon. It was established in 1953 and the extensive buildings and grounds comprise a mixture of older and newer structures. Kendra Hall was the former family home of Allders of Croydon and the main house currently houses Year 6, Year 2, the school library, computer suite, medical room and offices. Newer accommodation houses Reception, Year 1, Year 3, Year 4, and Year 5 are in our newest block opening in 1995.
Our Mission Statement
With the help of God's love, the Federation of St Elphege's and Regina Coeli Catholic schools will seek to develop the whole child. Each child is uniquely created and precious to God and it is the Federation's mission, guided by the Holy Spirit, to nurture each child's spiritual, moral and academic growth. Inspired by the teachings of Christ we will…

Safeguarding Statement
The Safeguarding Policy has clear procedures in place which all staff are aware of. Parents and carers are able to read the Policy on the school website and are free to discuss issues surrounding policy and practice with the Executive Headteacher, Deputy Headteacher or Chair of Governors. Sometimes we may need to share information and work in partnership with other agencies where there are concerns about a child’s welfare. We will ensure that our concerns are discussed with the parents/carers first unless we have reason to believe that such a move would be contrary to the child’s welfare.

Sancta Familia Catholic Academy Trust
On 1st February 2025, Regina Coeli Catholic Primary School joined the Sancta Familia Catholic Academy Trust, alongside St Elphege's Infant and Junior Schools.
Sancta Familia Catholic Academy Trust is a growing community of Catholic schools where faith, learning, and growth come together to inspire students toward excellence. All of our schools are committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment where every child feels valued and encouraged to achieve their personal best.

The Catholic Life of The School
Our School
Christmas at Regina Coeli
The last week of the Autumn term is always very exciting as we come together to celebrate approaching the birth of our Saviour, Jesus Christ!
The week began with members of our school choir visiting Haling Park Care Home to sing some Christmas songs. The children really enjoyed spending time with members of our local community and sharing some festive cheer with them!
KS2 came together for our annual Carol Service. Children from every class sang songs to retell the Christmas Story. We were so glad that we were able to return to St. Dominic's this year, and it was wonderful to share our celebration with so many members of our Regina Coeli families!
On the last day of term term, Father Martin came to say Mass for the whole school. We came together to give thanks for God's most precious gift as we prepare for the coming of Jesus.
Thank you to Father Simplicio, Father Martin and all of our Regina Coeli families for joining us to make our preparation for Christmas so special!
November 2022 - Remembrance Day
Today we joined in the two minutes silence and remembered those who have lost their lives in conflicts around the world during our Remembrance Day Assembly. Our School Parliament members shared their personal reflections on who they remember and we all thought about the children living in places of conflict around the world.
October 2022 - Harvest Mass
This October we were very happy to be able to hold our Harvest Mass. It was wonderful to be able to come together again in our shared love of our faith and invite parents to come and join us too!
The families at Regina Coeli were incredibly generous and we were overwhelmed with the donations made. Both the Purley Food Hub and Croydon Night Watch were very thankful for the support given by our school family.
We were also extremely grateful to Father. Simplicio from our parish of St. Dominic who came to say Mass for us! Thank you Father. Simplicio!
September 2022 - Macmillan Coffee Morning
A very big thank you to our Year 6 pupils who hosted our Macmillan Coffee Morning for parents! The morning started with a beautiful liturgy which was prepared and led by the pupils. This was followed by an opportunity for parents to share a slice of cake and a hot drink together.
Thanks to the immense generosity of our families we were able to raise £120 for Macmillan cancer support!
June 2022
RE Creativity Week and Feast Day Celebration
We ended June with our annual RE Creativity Week. This year, we studied different artistic representations of Mother Mary from around the world, and our pupils used them as inspiration for their own artwork. As you can see from the photos below, we have a very talented school of pupils here at Regina Coeli, and the work on their year group displays is stunning!
During RE Creativity Week, our Reception and KS2 took some time to reflect and wonder about Mary, her life and her role in our lives. They had lots of questions, so wrote letters to Mary to find out more about her! Our KS2 pupils took on the role of the teacher, and wrote back to the infants to let them know what they think Mary would have said in response. The children asked such insightful questions, and responded in such a thoughtful way - it really helped bring Mary to life for them!
At the ended of the week, we celebrated with our Feast Day Mass. Father Martin from St. Gertrude's parish and Father Simplicio from St. Dominic's parish said mass for us. Thank you Father Martin and Father Simplicio!
This was followed by the Regina Coeli Family Feast Day on our school field, where parents were invited to join us for lunch after the mass. It was wonderful to be able to hold our annual picnic again for the first time in a couple of years, and we are so appreciative of all the continued support from families, thank you!

May 2022
Year 6 Liturgy
Father Malachy from Holy Family's parish led a liturgy for our year 6 pupils this week. It was an opportunity for the children to reflect on all the hard work they have done this year, and to speak with the Lord in their hearts as they prepare to sit their SATs.
We are so proud of the pupils in St. Felicity and St. Dominic for their tremendous attitude towards learning!
Thank you Father Malachy!
April 2022
Give Thanks for the Risen Lord!
We began the summer term with a mass said by Father Simplicio from St. Dominic's parish. The mass celebrated the Risen Life of the Lord, and we gave thanks for Christ's sacrifice at this most holy and special time of year.
This mass was also very important to us because it was the first time we have been able to hold a whole school mass in a while! It was wonderful for all pupils and staff to be able to come together.
Thank you Father Simplicio!
March 2022
Preparing for Easter at Regina Coeli
In our final week of the spring term, we have been preparing for Easter. Reception and KS1 , and KS2, both led beautiful liturgies, sharing the story of Easter weekend. We shared scripture, prayer and song, and it was a wonderful opportunity to come together to celebrate and give thank for the sacrifice of our Lord, Jesus Christ.
We have also been learning about the act of Almsgiving during Lent, and will be raising money to support two very important causes: CAFOD's Walk for Hunger Campaign, and CAFOD's Ukraine Humanitarian Appeal. Since the beginning if Lent, pupils have been thinking about the sacrifices they will make during this time in order to raise money to support our global brothers and sisters. The children have designed their own donation envelopes, which we will be collecting when we return from the Easter break.
To end our week of preparation, each class participated in the journey around the stations of the cross, sharing prayer and scripture to reflect upon the pain and suffering Jesus experienced in order that our sins may be forgiven.
From our Regina Coeli family to yours, we hope you have a restful Easter.
Friday 4th March 2022
Thursday 6th January 2022 - Epiphany Mass
Today we were able to celebrate the Epiphany with a Mass specially recorded for us by Father Martin from St. Gertrude's Church. We hope that our school family enjoyed sharing the Mass with us at home too.
Thank you Father Martin!
Friday 17th December 2021
Today we celebrated the coming birth of our Lord, Jesus Christ, with a Mass specially live streamed for us by Father Simplicio from St. Dominic's Church.
We felt so fortunate that we were still able to celebrate Mass, and Kasia, one of our year 6 pupils, wrote a beautiful letter to Father Simplicio to express our thanks.
Thank you Father Simplicio!
November 2021 - Remembrance Day
On Thursday 11th November, we stopped at 11 o'clock for two minutes silence in memory of all those who have sacrificed their lives for us. On Remembrance Day, we came together in prayer as a mark of our respect for the fallen.
We would like to share with you the prayer we said together in school this morning.
Over the past couple of days we have been selling poppies to raise money for The Royal British Legion. Many thanks to all who have supported this cause.
October 2021 - Harvest Mass
This October we were very happy to be able to hold our Harvest Mass. It was wonderful to be able to come together again in our shared love of our faith and invite parents to come and join us too!
The families at Regina Coeli were incredibly generous and we were overwhelmed with the donations made. Both the Purley Food Hub and Regina Coeli Food Hub were very thankful for the support given by our school family.
We were also extremely grateful to Father. Martin from our parish of St. Gertrude who came to say Mass for us! Thank you Father. Martin!
September 2021 - Macmillan Coffee Morning
A very big thank you to our Year 6 pupils who hosted our Macmillan Coffee Morning for parents! The morning started with a beautiful liturgy which was prepared and led by the pupils. This was followed by an opportunity for parents to share a slice of cake and a hot drink together, before a further cake sale at the end of the day.
Thanks to the immense generosity of our families we were able to raise £290 for Macmillan Cancer support!
July 2021 - Creativity Week
He who sings prays twice!
In the summer term we had our annual RE Creativity Week. As we had missed singing together so much during the pandemic, we decided that the theme of the week should be based around some of our favourite hymns! In our year groups we spent the week completing differenct actvities based around our hymns and lots of singing, as well as creating these beautiful displays! Can you guess the hymns we chose to celebrate?

Sutton Catholic School Alliance (SCSA)
There are eight families of schools in the Sutton Catholic School Alliance (SCSA) who are committed to working together in a variety of ways; at leadership and governance level and with teaching and support staff to improve the studens' experience and secure the future of Catholic education in the London Borough of Sutton.
Work is rooted in the seven principles of Catholic Social Teaching (CST).
The SCSA will further develop their partnership through joint work focusing specifically on:
Leadership development and succession planning.
CPD for all staff.
Efficiency savings.
Recruitment at all levels.
Faith Formation.

Our Curriculum
Learning
Our Curriculum
We believe that quality first teaching paired with a coherent curriculum is the key to success for our pupils. We value and celebrate the culturally diverse community we serve and hope to draw on their wealth of talent, skills and knowledge. Our school motto is Where there is Love, there is God and pupils are introduced to the idea of service, both to the school and wider community, through the example of Mary our mother.
At Regina Coeli, our vision is to develop a community where our school will be a place of excellence, where all staff recognise their position of trust and their responsibilities towards the children in their care. Our curriculum is designed to be knowledge-rich, enquiry based, ambitious for all our pupils and literacy centred and is underpinned by the National Curriculum.
Knowledge Rich: We intend for our pupils to achieve powerful knowledge that gradually increases in complexity so that pupils develop a deep and embedded understanding of the different subjects they study.
Enquiry Based: Our vision is that our children achieve agency as independent learners and through our curriculum, we ignite their intellectual curiosity. We believe that effective questioning is a fundamental part of successful learning and progress; this plays a crucial role in every classroom. The curriculum is designed to facilitate the essential principles of mastery, identifying key knowledge, breaking it down into smaller steps until the learning is achieved.
Ambitious for All: Our pupils are entitled to a broad and balanced curriculum. We plan for all pupils to access regardless of their starting points. This helps them to make sense of the world in which they live, contribute positively to society and be ready for their next stage of learning.
Literacy Centred: We understand the power of story and how the brain privileges narrative therefore high quality literature is central to our curriculum. We make purposeful choices about the books our pupils read so that they can contextualise their learning, foster a love of reading and enhance their acquisition of vocabulary.
Through a research informed approach our curriculum planning is dynamic so that our pupils receive the highest quality provision.
With the help of God's love, the school seeks to develop the whole child. Each child is uniquely created and precious to God and it is our mission, guided by the Holy Spirit, to nurture each child's spiritual, moral and academic growth.
If you would like to know more about any aspect of our curriculum, please speak with your child's class teacher or contact a member of the leadership team through the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND | Regina Coeli Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND
Parent Information
SEND at Our School
At Regina Coeli Primary School we ensure that as far as possible all children have access to a broad and balanced curriculum, and have equal opportunity to an education that is appropriate to their needs. Our teachers adapt their planning to meet the needs of children in their class so that individuals make progress. The children are given regular opportunities to evaluate their learning and may be involved in setting future targets. We develop a partnership with parents and carers so that their knowledge, views and experience can assist us in assessing and providing for their child.
Our school it part of an exciting initiative by Croydon Council to improve support for children with special needs or disabilities (SEND) who live in Croydon.
We are working with a cluster of local schools, who together have been given funding to provide early intervention and better targeted help to support children and young people with SEND. This will enable our special needs staff to work closely with our partner schools to quickly get the necessary support and help for pupils who are beginning to demonstrate that they have additional needs which cannot be met through our own school SEND resources.
This early help may be in the form of advice, school to school support, referral to specialist services, or additional resources. The support can be put in place rapidly without unnecessary delay. This is because our group of schools manage the funding between us so we can direct this to the most suitable children in an efficient targeted way. If, despite this rapid support it is thought that a child would still benefit from an Education and Health Care Plan the local group will work together to ensure that the application to assess is submitted promptly with all the relevant information including from outside professionals.
The initiative is called “Locality SEND Support” and will run throughout this academic year. We will of course monitor the outcomes closely and we will always involve parents and carers in any decisions made and review the support regularly. Presently the scheme is only for Croydon residents and will not impact on students who already have an Education & Health Care Plan or those in Enhanced Learning Provisions.
If you want to learn more about this scheme, please contact our SENDCo and we will be happy to provide you with you further details.
Mrs Spain, Deputy Head Teacher and SENDCo, can be contacted through the school office.

Early Years Information
Parent Information
Nursery
Our Nursery is led by qualified staff and follows the Government's Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum. We offer morning sessions from 8.30am - 11.30am and afternoon sessions from 12.15pm - 3.15pm. We also offer full-time places.
Part time places are fully funded by the government's Free Early Universal Education Offer which provides free nursery education for children over 9 months old for 15 hours per week.
Some families are entitled to 30 hours' free childcare per week. To find out whether you might be eligible and to register for funding please click here.
The 30 hours funding is subject to eligibility criteria determined by the government. If you are offered a full day place and accept this but subsequently cease to be eligible during the year you would need to pay the school for all sessions not funded by the government. If you are not eligible for 30 hours, we do also offer the option of paying for a full time session.
We can also offer a lunch consisting of a sandwich / wrap / pasta bowl, fresh fruit / vegetable sticks and flapjack / yogurt / cake at a weekly cost of £14. Alternatively, you can provide a nut free healthy packed lunch for your child.
If you would like to apply for Nursery please complete this Admission Administration Form below and return it with a copy of your child's birth certificate to the school office.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium & PE/Sports Grant
Parent Information
Pupil Premium & PE/Sports Grant
Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011, and paid by means of a specific grant based on school census figures for pupils registered as eligible for FSM in reception to Year 11. For looked after children the Pupil Premium was calculated using the Children Looked After data returns (SSDA903).
A premium has also been introduced for children whose parents are currently serving in the armed forces. This service premium is designed to address the emotional and social well-being of these pupils. The Pupil Premium is additional to main school funding and it will be used by this school to address any underlying inequalities between children eligible by ensuring that funding reaches the pupils who need it most.
PE & Sport Premium
The Government is providing additional in order to improve the provision of physical education and sport in primary schools. This funding is being jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport, and will see money going directly to schools to be spent on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children. All state-maintained schools, academies, middle schools, special schools and pupil referral units which have primary aged pupils (as reported in the 2013 school census) will receive the funding.

National Literacy Trust
Over the next days, weeks and months the National Literacy Trust will be updating their sites as often as they can with new and useful content for parents. Split up by age group below, you will find ideas and guidance for simple activities that will engage your children at home, while also benefiting their reading, writing and language development. You'll be able to access free reading and writing resources, audiobooks, videos, competitions and reading challenges. Every resource is available for free, although to access some you may need to create a free account.
